summary: GeoIris (Earth Science Change Detective & Significance Engine) is an interactive Earth-science platform developed by Team Quasar Crew to address the challenge of detecting environmental changes, analysing trends, and evaluating their statistical significance. It integrates NASA Earth-observation data and reanalysis resources with geographic visualization, time-series analysis, and advanced statistical computing to investigate what is changing, where it is happening, and how significant those changes are. Users can explore multi-decadal environmental patterns, remove seasonal fluctuations, apply statistical methods such as Mann-Kendall, Theil-Sen, and OLS regression, and compare contrasting regional trends. Beyond trend analysis, GeoIris provides interactive environmental investigations, custom data ingestion, forecasting, Bayesian modelling, wildfire monitoring, SAR-based change detection, and geospatial raster analysis. By connecting satellite observations, scientific computation, and accessible interpretation in one platform, GeoIris makes rigorous Earth-system investigation more accessible to students, researchers, educators, and citizen scientists.
details:
PROJECT DETAILS

GeoIris (Earth Science Change Detective & Significance Engine) is an interactive Earth-science intelligence platform developed by Team Quasar Crew. It was designed to transform complex Earth-observation data into interpretable, statistically tested, and geographically meaningful scientific evidence.

HOW IT WORKS

GeoIris connects Earth-observation data, geographic exploration, statistical analysis, and advanced computational methods through an integrated web-based environment.

Users can investigate environmental variables such as surface air temperature, precipitation, vegetation greenness (NDVI), soil moisture, evapotranspiration, aerosol optical depth, land surface temperature, and ozone. The platform integrates NASA data services and Earth-observation resources, including NASA POWER, MODIS, VIIRS, FIRMS, MERRA-2, GIBS, Earthdata CMR, EONET, and ASF catalogue services.

Its interactive global map allows users to explore predefined environmental regions or investigate custom geographic coordinates. Monthly observations are transformed into time series, with climatological normalization and deseasonalization helping distinguish long-term environmental patterns from recurring seasonal fluctuations.

The statistical engine applies Ordinary Least Squares regression, Mann-Kendall trend testing, Theil-Sen slope estimation, Student's t-tests, confidence intervals, and additional statistical diagnostics. These methods help evaluate trend direction, magnitude, uncertainty, and statistical significance.

GeoIris also investigates regional contrasts through synchronized comparisons, allowing users to examine how similar environmental processes can produce different outcomes across geographic locations.

THE SEVEN INTEGRATED MODULES

  1. Trend Explorer: Investigates environmental variables through interactive maps, time-series visualizations, deseasonalized anomalies, regression models, and statistical significance testing.
  2. Data Detective: Converts environmental investigations into interactive scientific missions, allowing learners to examine satellite evidence, solve environmental mysteries, and develop scientific interpretations.
  3. Opposite Trends Lab: Compares environmental indicators across different regions to investigate contrasting trends and geographic differences in Earth-system behaviour.
  4. Encyclopedia: Provides a searchable scientific reference for environmental variables, satellite missions, Earth-observation datasets, and related concepts.
  5. Custom Data: Supports geographic data retrieval through NASA services and the import of user-provided CSV and JSON datasets for further analysis.
  6. Statistical Lab: Provides advanced inferential statistics, regression techniques, multivariate analysis, autocorrelation-adjusted trend testing, change-point detection, extreme-value analysis, and residual diagnostics.
  7. Earth Compute Lab: Extends the platform into advanced computational Earth science through time-series forecasting, Bayesian MCMC, extreme-value modelling, spatial false-discovery-rate analysis, SAR change detection, DEM differencing, land-cover transition analysis, and scientific raster processing.

ADVANCED COMPUTATIONAL CAPABILITIES

The Python backend provides computational workflows beyond conventional environmental dashboards.

These include SARIMAX forecasting with prediction intervals and backtesting, Bayesian adaptive MCMC with convergence diagnostics, Generalized Extreme Value and Generalized Pareto modelling, and spatial Mann-Kendall analysis with multiple-testing corrections.

Geospatial processing includes adaptive Lee speckle filtering, SAR log-ratio change detection, Digital Elevation Model differencing, erosion and deposition volume estimation, and land-cover transition matrices.

The platform also supports scientific data inspection and extraction through NetCDF4, HDF5, and xarray.

DATA INTEGRITY AND SCIENTIFIC CONSIDERATIONS

Scientific reliability was a central consideration throughout development. GeoIris distinguishes satellite observations, reanalysis products, user-provided datasets, and synthetic demonstrations through explicit provenance classifications.

It preserves missing satellite observations as null values instead of automatically treating them as zero, helping avoid misleading interpretations. Its analytical design also considers seasonal variability, extreme observations, temporal autocorrelation, uncertainty, multiple statistical comparisons, and the limitations of individual datasets.

Some authenticated NASA workflows require optional credentials, while certain computational modules provide clearly identified synthetic demonstration scenarios when actual input data or credentials are unavailable.

INTENDED BENEFITS AND IMPACT

GeoIris aims to make advanced Earth-system investigation more accessible to students, researchers, educators, and environmental practitioners.

By bringing geographic visualization, statistical inference, satellite observations, and computational analysis together, it reduces the fragmentation often encountered when working with multiple Earth-science tools.

Its educational capabilities encourage data literacy and scientific reasoning, while its analytical capabilities support environmental monitoring, climate research, regional comparisons, wildfire investigation, and geospatial change assessment.

The long-term vision is to provide an extensible environment where users can move from discovering environmental changes to testing their significance, investigating their geographic context, and communicating their findings through reproducible scientific outputs.

TECHNOLOGIES AND DEVELOPMENT TOOLS

Frontend:

  • React 19
  • TypeScript
  • Vite
  • Tailwind CSS
  • Leaflet
  • Chart.js
  • React Chart.js 2
  • Lucide React
  • Simple Statistics
  • ML-Matrix

Backend and Scientific Computing:

  • Python 3.12+
  • FastAPI
  • NumPy
  • pandas
  • SciPy
  • statsmodels
  • scikit-learn
  • scikit-image
  • xarray
  • NetCDF4
  • h5netcdf
  • Rasterio
  • tifffile
  • Shapely
  • earthaccess
  • Requests
  • HTTPX

Development and Deployment:

  • GitHub
  • Docker
  • Vercel
  • REST APIs
  • NASA Earth-observation services

GeoIris was developed as a web-based software platform. No specialized hardware requirement is necessary for its standard browser-based exploration interface.

CREATIVITY AND INNOVATION

The central creative idea behind GeoIRIS is to transform Earth observation from passive visualization into active scientific investigation.

Rather than simply displaying whether an environmental variable has increased or decreased, the platform encourages users to investigate where the change occurred, how large it was, whether it is statistically significant, and how its behaviour differs across regions.

Its combination of interactive environmental mysteries, opposite regional trend comparisons, robust statistical methods, advanced geospatial computation, and reproducible reporting creates a multidisciplinary approach to Earth-system investigation.

The platform also bridges educational accessibility and advanced scientific computing, allowing beginners to explore environmental evidence while providing more experienced users with sophisticated analytical workflows.

CONCLUSION

GeoIris seeks to bridge the gap between Earth-observation data and meaningful scientific understanding. By integrating NASA resources, geographic intelligence, statistical evidence, and computational Earth science into one environment, it provides a practical approach to investigating the changing Earth.

Developed by Team Quasar Crew for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, GeoIris is built around one central objective: making environmental change detectable, measurable, testable, and understandable.
